Error.description: The request was refused or failed. The body lists every fault found.

action.description: What was done, such as pr_created or branch_pushed, or what was refused or failed, such as git_denied or branch_push_failed.

actor_name.description: The name of the person in actor_user_id, set only on the organization's actions feed.

actor_user_id.description: The id of the person who took, authorized, or started the work behind the action, absent when no person did.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation the action was taken for, absent when it was taken for none or the conversation was deleted.

credential.description: The organization credential the action was taken with: github_app, github_pat, jira_org, linear_org, slack_bot, or none when it used none.

details.description: JSON details particular to the action, such as the commit sha of a branch push, absent when there are none.

external_id.description: The outside system's own id for the object the action was on, such as a pull request number or a comment id, absent when none was recorded.

from_state.description: The state a transition moved the object from, such as a Jira status, absent when the action is not a transition.

object_id.description: The id of the object the action changed, the value an artifact's object_id carries, absent when it changed none or the object cannot be identified.

object_kind.description: The kind of object the action changed, such as pull_request, branch, or comment, absent when it changed none.

occurred_at.description: When the action was taken, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

performed_by.description: Who performed the action: agent, person, or system.

provider.description: The outside system the action was on: github, jira, linear, slack, or network for a refused network connection.

scope.description: Where in that system the action was: the GitHub host, the Jira site, the Linear workspace id, slack.com, or internet for a refused network connection.

target.description: The key of what the action was on, as the action named it, such as owner/repo#42, owner/repo, or PROJ-123.

team_id.description: The id of the team whose conversation took the action, set only on the organization's actions feed and absent there for an action with no team.

team_name.description: That team's name, set only on the organization's actions feed.

to_state.description: The state a transition moved the object to, absent when the action is not a transition.

url.description: The page of the object the action was on, under the object's current name, absent when none was recorded.

message.description: On a deny, the reason the agent is given, which may be empty.

updated_input.description: On an allow, the tool input the agent runs the call with in place of its own; absent or null runs the call with the agent's input.

permission.description: The answered prompt, absent when no record of it could be read.

kind.description: The kind of deliverable: pull_request or review.

state.description: Where the deliverable stands: pending, draft, open, merged, or closed for a pull request, and pending, submitted, or dismissed for a review.

action_count.description: How many actions the conversation took on the object.

deliverable.description: The conversation's deliverable that is this object, or null when none is.

entity_id.description: The id of the entity the object is or is on, absent when it is on none.

first_at.description: When the conversation first acted on the object, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

last_action.description: The newest action the conversation took on the object, such as pr_created or branch_pushed.

last_at.description: When the conversation last acted on the object, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

name.description: The object's name within its repository for a branch, label, release, workflow, or workflow run, and empty for every other kind.

object_id.description: The object's id, which the conversation's actions list takes as object_id.

object_kind.description: The kind of object: pull_request, issue, repository, branch, label, release, workflow, workflow_run, review, comment, or message.

provider.description: The outside system the object is in, such as github, jira, linear, or slack.

scope.description: Where in that system the object is: the GitHub host, the Jira site, the Linear workspace id, or slack.com.

target.description: The key of the object, or of the entity it is on, such as owner/repo#42 or PROJ-123, kept current through renames.

url.description: The object's page in its system, empty when no action recorded one.

completed_at.description: When the check run completed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or an empty string until it does.

conclusion.description: How a completed check run ended: success, failure, cancelled, timed_out, action_required, neutral, skipped, or stale; an empty string until it completes.

id.description: GitHub's id for the check run.

status.description: The check run's status: queued, in_progress, or completed.

workflow_run_id.description: The id of the GitHub Actions workflow run the check belongs to, absent for a check from any other system.

failing.description: How many completed as failure, timed_out, cancelled, or action_required.

passing.description: How many completed without failing or being skipped.

total.description: How many check runs there are.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

file.description: The file of a file block, absent on any other block.

image_url.description: The image of an image_url block, absent on any other block.

text.description: The text of a text block, absent on any other block.

type.description: The kind of block: text, image_url, or file.

file_data.description: The file's contents, absent when file_url or file_id gives the file.

file_id.description: The model provider's id for the file, absent when file_data or file_url gives the file.

file_type.description: The file's media type, absent when none is recorded.

file_url.description: The file's URL, absent when file_data or file_id gives the file.

filename.description: The file's name, absent when none is recorded.

detail.description: The level of detail the model reads the image at, such as low or high, absent for the provider's default.

file_id.description: The model provider's id for the image file, absent when url gives the image.

url.description: The image's URL, which may be a data: URI, absent when file_id names the image.

object_id.description: The object_id of one of the conversation's artifacts, to return only the actions that changed that object; absent or empty applies no object filter.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

refused.description: Whether to return only the actions that were refused or failed.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

action_count.description: How many actions on outside systems the conversation recorded, refused and failed ones included.

actor_agent_id.description: The id of the agent the conversation runs as, empty when none is recorded.

actor_agent_name.description: The display name of that agent, empty when actor_agent_id is empty or the agent was deleted.

artifact_count.description: How many objects in outside systems the conversation changed.

artifact_counts.description: How many objects the conversation changed, keyed by object kind, such as pull_request or branch, and an empty object when it changed none.

blueprint_run_id.description: The id of the blueprint run the conversation is a step of, empty when it is not a step.

blueprint_run_status.description: The status of the conversation's blueprint run: running, completed, aborted, failed, or cancelled, empty when it is not a step or the run could not be read.

blueprint_step_count.description: How many steps the conversation's blueprint run has, 0 when it is not a step or the run could not be read.

blueprint_step_index.description: The conversation's step in its blueprint run, counted from 0, or null when it is not a step.

cache_creation_tokens.description: How many input tokens the conversation's model calls wrote to the provider's prompt cache.

cache_read_tokens.description: How many input tokens the conversation's model calls read from the provider's prompt cache.

cache_warm_until.description: When the model provider's prompt cache from the newest assistant turn expires, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent from the conversation list and when the conversation has no assistant turn.

can_write.description: Whether the caller may stop the conversation, message it, and answer its permission prompts, absent when the check fails.

claim_current_op.description: The operation that engagement had in flight at its last report, absent when no engagement holds the conversation or it has not reported yet.

claim_last_activity_at.description: When the engagement running the conversation last reported activity, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when no engagement holds the conversation or it has not reported yet.

claimed_at.description: When work on the conversation last started, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when it never has.

completed_at.description: When the conversation's last engagement finished, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when none has.

current_action.description: A sentence saying what a running conversation is doing, present only on the conversation list and only when there is something to say.

duration_ms.description: How long the conversation's engagements have spent working, in milliseconds, or null before any time is recorded.

ended_at.description: When the conversation stopped being its task's current conversation, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent while it still is.

ended_reason.description: Why the conversation stopped being its task's current conversation, such as requeued, delegated, or taken_over, present exactly when ended_at is.

failure_kind.description: What made a failed conversation fail, such as memory_limit, crash, or executor_lost, empty when it has not failed or the failure was not classified.

has_run.description: Whether the conversation holds an assistant turn.

has_unresolved_deliverables.description: Whether a draft pull request or a ready review the conversation prepared still waits on a person, absent when the conversation's deliverables could not be read.

input_tokens.description: How many input tokens the conversation's model calls used.

memory_missing.description: Whether the agent has not written its own memory of the conversation.

model.description: The model the conversation runs on, empty before one is chosen.

next_attempt_at.description: The earliest time the conversation is picked up again after its model provider was unavailable, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when nothing is holding it back.

next_message_effort.description: The reasoning effort a message that names none would run at, present with next_message_model unless it is the provider's default.

next_message_model.description: The model a message that names none would run on, absent from the conversation list and when such a message would be refused.

num_turns.description: How many turns the conversation's engagements have run, or null before any are recorded.

outcome.description: The verdict the agent reported when it stopped: continue, finish, or abort, empty when it reported none.

outcome_reason.description: Why the agent stopped and what a person needs to do, empty when it gave no reason.

output_tokens.description: How many output tokens the conversation's model calls produced.

park_reason.description: Why the conversation was parked open, such as user_cancelled, stalled, or launch_failed, empty when it is not parked or has resumed since.

pending_deliverable_ids.description: The ids of the draft pull requests and ready reviews that still wait on a person, an empty array when none do, and absent when the conversation's deliverables could not be read.

prompt_id.description: The id of the prompt the conversation was started with, empty when it was started with none.

queue_position.description: The conversation's place in its organization's queue, counted from 1, present only on the conversation list and only while it waits in line.

queued_at.description: When the conversation last entered the queue, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when it never has.

result_summary.description: The agent's account of what it did, empty until it gives one.

resumable.description: Whether a message sent now would continue the conversation, absent from the conversation list and for a conversation that is active or failed.

resume_blocked_reason.description: Why a message sent now would not continue the conversation, such as workspace_expired or blueprint_concluded, present exactly when resumable is false.

runtime.description: The engine that runs the conversation: sdk or native.

session_id.description: The Claude Code session id a conversation on the sdk runtime resumes with, empty when it has none.

started_at.description: When the conversation was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

status.description: The conversation's displayed status: queued, running, open, or failed, or, while an engagement is setting up, its phase: fetching, cloning, agent_starting, or awaiting_credentials.

stop_requested_at.description: When a stop that has not taken effect yet was requested, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when no stop is pending.

task_id.description: The id of the task the conversation works on.

total_cost_usd.description: What the conversation's model calls have cost, in USD, or null before any cost is recorded.

trigger_id.description: The id of the event handler whose firing started the conversation, empty for a manual one.

trigger_type.description: How the conversation was started: manual or event.

type.description: What the conversation is for: delegation for agent work, or interactive for the conversation a person's claim of the task started.

unresolved_pr_count.description: How many draft pull requests the conversation prepared still wait on a person, absent when the conversation's deliverables could not be read.

unresolved_review_count.description: How many ready reviews the conversation prepared still wait on a person, absent when the conversation's deliverables could not be read.

worktree_path.description: The path of the conversation's run directory on the host that ran it, empty before it has one.

attention.description: Whether to return only the conversations waiting on a person: those with an unanswered permission prompt, and those neither running nor setting up that still hold a draft pull request or a ready review waiting on a person.

entity_ids.description: The ids of the entities whose tasks' conversations to return, at most 200; absent or empty applies no entity filter.

include_messages.description: Whether to return, as messages, the transcript of the newest conversation of each task on the page.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

statuses.description: The displayed statuses to return, from queued, running, open, failed, fetching, cloning, agent_starting, and awaiting_credentials; absent or empty returns every status.

task_ids.description: The ids of the tasks whose conversations to return, at most 500; absent or empty applies no task filter.

team_ids.description: The ids of the teams whose conversations to return, at most 100; absent or empty applies no team filter.

messages.description: The transcript of each task's newest conversation on the page, keyed by conversation id, oldest message first, present only when include_messages is true and a transcript holds a message.

next_page_token.description: The token that reads the next page, as page_token, absent on the last page.

runs.description: The page's conversations, keyed by task id, each task's newest first; an empty object when the page holds none.

total_count.description: How many conversations match the filters, across every page.

effort.description: The reasoning effort the message runs at: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max; absent or null runs it at the effort the conversation's next_message_effort names, or the provider's default when that is absent.

model.description: The model the message runs on, one this deployment offers; absent or null runs it on the model the conversation's next_message_model names.

text.description: The message, which must not be blank.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation that raised the prompt.

decided_at.description: When the prompt was answered, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent while it is pending.

decided_by.description: The id of the person who answered the prompt, absent when no person did.

expires_at.description: When the prompt's window was due to end, as projected when it was raised, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when none was recorded.

input.description: The input the agent asked to call the tool with, absent when it is not known.

org_id.description: The id of the organization the prompt belongs to.

reason.description: Why the prompt reached its state: user when a person answered it, timeout when no answer came within its window, absent when no one was present to answer it, closing when the conversation ended under it, or claim_lost when the engagement that asked went away; the key is left out while the prompt is pending.

requested_at.description: When the agent asked, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

state.description: Where the prompt stands: pending, allowed, denied, or expired.

title.description: The prompt's text as the agent runtime wrote it, absent when it wrote none.

tool_call_id.description: The id of the tool call the prompt asked about.

tool_name.description: The name of the tool the agent asked to call.

waited_ms.description: How long the prompt stood open before it was answered, in milliseconds, absent while it is pending.

draft.description: With true, converts the pull request to a draft on GitHub; with false, marks it ready for review. It is required, and null is refused.

count.description: How many of the caller's pull requests merged that day.

date.description: The day, as a YYYY-MM-DD date in UTC.

awaiting.description: How many of the caller's pull requests are open and ready for review.

closed.description: How many of the caller's pull requests closed without merging within the window.

draft.description: How many of the caller's pull requests are open drafts.

merged.description: How many of the caller's pull requests merged within the window.

merged_over_time.description: How many of the caller's pull requests merged on each of the last 14 days, oldest first, counting only merges within the window; null when the caller has no GitHub identity bound.

reviews_given.description: How many reviews the caller has left on other people's pull requests.

reviews_received.description: How many reviews other people have left on the caller's pull requests.

event.description: The event the review was submitted with: APPROVE, COMMENT, or REQUEST_CHANGES, set for a review deliverable.

html_url.description: The pull request's page on GitHub, set for a pull request deliverable.

number.description: The pull request's number, set for a pull request deliverable.

review_id.description: The id GitHub gave the submitted review, set for a review deliverable.

state.description: The deliverable's state after the approval: open for a pull request, submitted for a review.

url.description: The submitted review's page on GitHub, set for a review deliverable.

html_url.description: The pull request's page on GitHub.

number.description: The pull request's number, or 0 when the deliverable names no pull request.

state.description: The deliverable's state after the dismissal: closed.

body.description: The pull request's new body; absent or null keeps the current body.

title.description: The pull request's new title, trimmed of surrounding whitespace, which may not be empty; absent or null keeps the current title.

updated.description: How many of the conversation's pull requests changed state.

branch.description: The name of the head branch deleted from the repository.

html_url.description: The pull request's page on GitHub.

state.description: The deliverable's state after the rejection: closed.

cve_id.description: The advisory's CVE id, absent when it has none.

first_patched_version.description: The first version that fixes the advisory, absent when none has been released.

ghsa_id.description: The advisory's GitHub Security Advisory id.

manifest_path.description: The path of the manifest file that declares the package.

number.description: The alert's number in its repository.

scope.description: Whether the dependency is runtime or development, absent when GitHub does not know.

severity.description: The advisory's severity: low, medium, high, or critical.

summary.description: The advisory's summary, to be shown as plain text, absent when the advisory has none.

vulnerable_version_range.description: The range of versions the advisory affects, absent when GitHub reports none.

closed_at.description: When the entity closed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null while it is active.

created_at.description: When the entity was first recorded, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

kind.description: The kind of entity: pr, issue, vulnerable_package, thread, or message.

latest_event_at.description: When the entity's newest event was recorded, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when it has none.

latest_event_type.description: The type of the entity's newest recorded event, or null when it has none.

mine.description: Whether the entity is a pull request the caller's GitHub identity on the organization's host wrote; false for every other kind of entity.

pull_request.description: A pull request's fields as its last poll read them, or null for every other kind of entity and for a pull request no poll has read yet.

repository_id.description: The id of a GitHub entity's repository, which a rename of the repository does not change, or null for an entity from any other source.

source.description: The system the entity comes from: github, jira, linear, or slack.

source_id.description: The entity's key in its source, such as owner/repo#42 for a pull request or PROJ-123 for a Jira issue.

state.description: Whether the entity is active or closed.

url.description: The entity's page in its source.

closed_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that leaves out entities that closed before it; an entity that has not closed is included.

ids.description: Ids of the entities to include, at most 200, each a UUID in lowercase hyphenated form; empty includes every entity.

kinds.description: Kinds of entity to include, from issue, message, pr, thread, and vulnerable_package; empty includes every kind.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

sources.description: Sources whose entities to include, from github, jira, linear, and slack; empty includes every source.

states.description: States to include, from active and closed; empty includes both.

team_ids.description: Ids of the teams, at most 100, whose tracked repositories, projects, teams, and channels limit the result; empty uses every team the caller belongs to, and a team the caller is not on matches nothing.

additions.description: How many lines the pull request adds.

author.description: The GitHub login of the pull request's author.

deletions.description: How many lines the pull request removes.

draft.description: Whether the pull request is a draft.

number.description: The pull request's number in its repository.

errors.description: Every fault found in the request, at least one.

field.description: The request field at fault, present only when the fault is in one field.

message.description: A description of the fault for a person to read.

reason.description: A stable machine code for the fault, in upper snake case, such as INVALID_FIELD.

created_at.description: When the event was recorded, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

dedup_key.description: The value that tells apart events of one type on one entity, such as a label name, or an empty string for most event types.

entity_id.description: The id of the entity the event happened on.

event_type.description: The event's type, such as github:pr:ci_check_failed.

occurred_at.description: When the event happened in its source, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, such as a commit's or a review's time, or null when the source reported none.

entity_ids.description: Ids of the entities whose events to include, at most 200, each a UUID in lowercase hyphenated form; empty includes the events of every entity the caller may read.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

per_entity.description: The most events to include for each entity, its newest, from 1 to 200; absent includes every event.

since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to events recorded at or after it.

count.description: How many rows have the value.

value.description: The value the rows are counted by.

can_write.description: Whether the caller may approve, reject, dismiss, or edit the deliverable, absent when the check fails.

created_at.description: When the deliverable was recorded, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

details.description: The deliverable's kind-specific content as a JSON object, or null when it has none: from GET /api/deliverables/{id}, a pull request's owner, repo, number, head_branch, base_branch, title, and body, with the title and body read from GitHub when it answers, or a review's owner, repo, pr_number, review_body, review_event, comments, and commits_since_finalize; in a conversation's deliverables list, the stored content, whose fields include head_branch, base, proposed, snapshot, and resolution for a pull request and review_body, review_event, staged_comments, proposed, and resolution for a review.

external_id.description: The object's id on GitHub: the pull request's number, or the submitted review's id, empty while the object does not exist on GitHub.

kind.description: What the deliverable is: pull_request or review.

provider.description: The system the deliverable's object is on: github.

scope.description: The base URL of the GitHub the deliverable's object is on.

state.description: Where the deliverable is in its lifecycle: pending, draft, open, merged, or closed for a pull request, and pending, submitted, or dismissed for a review.

target.description: The pull request the deliverable is or reviews, as owner/repo#number.

url.description: The object's page on GitHub, empty while the object does not exist on GitHub.

error_kind.description: Why the attempt failed, present only when outcome is failed.

error_message.description: A description of the failure, present only when outcome is failed.

outcome.description: What the attempt came to: generated, empty, or failed, absent while it is running.

started_at.description: When the attempt started, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

cache_creation_tokens.description: How many input tokens that model call wrote to the provider's prompt cache, absent when none are recorded.

cache_read_tokens.description: How many input tokens that model call read from the provider's prompt cache, absent when none are recorded.

content_blocks.description: The message's images and files, absent when its text is its whole content.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation the message belongs to.

cost_usd.description: The cost of the model calls settled at this message, in USD, absent when the message settles none.

created_at.description: When the message was written, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

duration_ms.description: How long the work the message records took, in milliseconds, absent when it was not measured.

input_tokens.description: How many input tokens the model call that wrote the message used, absent when none are recorded.

is_error.description: Whether a tool message reports a failed call, absent when it does not.

metadata.description: Further details the agent runtime recorded on the message, absent when there are none.

model.description: The model that wrote an assistant message, or the model a person's message runs on, absent when none is recorded.

output_tokens.description: How many output tokens the model call that wrote the message produced, absent when none are recorded.

reasoning.description: The model's recorded reasoning for the message, absent when there is none.

role.description: Who the message is from: assistant, user, tool, or system.

stop_reason.description: Why the model provider ended the turn the message records, in the provider's spelling, such as end_turn or max_tokens, absent when it reported none.

subtype.description: A code naming a message that is not an ordinary turn, such as injection:memory for a note the system wrote into the transcript; empty for an assistant turn, a tool result, or a person's message.

tool_call_id.description: On a tool message, the id of the tool call it answers, absent on any other message.

tool_calls.description: The tool calls an assistant message makes, absent when it makes none.

auto_merge.description: Whether auto-merge is enabled on the pull request.

check_runs.description: The check runs on the pull request's head commit, the latest run of each check name.

checks_status.description: How many of check_runs are in each state.

conflicts.description: Whether the pull request has merge conflicts, which is when mergeable_state is dirty.

mergeable.description: Whether GitHub can merge the pull request, or null while GitHub is still computing it.

mergeable_state.description: GitHub's mergeable state, such as clean, dirty, blocked, behind, or unknown.

review_decision.description: The decision the reviews add up to: approved, changes_requested, review_required, or an empty string when there is none.

reviews.description: Each reviewer's latest approval, change request, or dismissal, in no particular order; null when there is none.

author.description: The GitHub login of the pull request's author.

created_at.description: When the pull request was opened, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

draft.description: Whether the pull request is a draft.

entity_id.description: The id of the pull request's entity, which the per-pull-request routes take.

html_url.description: The pull request's page on GitHub.

labels.description: The names of the pull request's labels.

number.description: The pull request's number in its repository.

state.description: The pull request's state: open, merged, or closed.

updated_at.description: When the pull request last changed on GitHub, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

body.description: The review's new summary body, trimmed of surrounding whitespace, which may not be empty; absent or null keeps the current body.

event.description: The event the review is to be submitted with: APPROVE, COMMENT, or REQUEST_CHANGES; absent or null keeps the current event.

state.description: Set to dismissed, the only value accepted, to abandon the pending review; it may not be sent with body or event, and absent or null leaves the review pending.

input.description: The input the agent wants to call the tool with, an empty object when it is not known.

requested_at.description: When the agent asked, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

timeout_ms.description: How long the prompt has left before it is denied for want of an answer, in milliseconds, or 0 when that is not known.

title.description: The prompt's text as the agent runtime wrote it, absent when it wrote none.

tool_call_id.description: The id of the tool call the prompt asks about, which the answer route takes in its path.

tool_name.description: The name of the tool the agent wants to call.

draft.description: With true, only drafts; with false, only pull requests ready for review; absent or null includes both.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

sort_dir.description: The direction of sort_key, asc or desc, desc when absent; it is refused without sort_key.

sort_key.description: Orders the result by updated_at, GitHub's last-activity time, with a pull request that has none last; absent orders it by when TF last polled each pull request, newest first.

states.description: States to include, from open, merged, and closed; empty includes every state.

data.description: The entry in the encrypted form the model provider returned, absent when it returned none.

index.description: The entry's position among the message's reasoning entries.

signature.description: A token the model provider issued with the entry to verify it, absent when it issued none.

text.description: The reasoning text, absent when the provider returned none.

type.description: The kind of reasoning entry, in the model provider's spelling.

base_branch.description: The branch agents base their work on, absent when they use the default branch.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller may change the repository's settings.

clone_error.description: The output of the failed clone, present only when clone_status is failed.

clone_error_kind.description: What kind of failure the clone hit, ssh or other, present only when clone_status is failed.

clone_status.description: The state of the repository's clone: pending until a clone attempt finishes, then ok or failed.

default_branch.description: The repository's default branch on GitHub, absent before it is profiled.

description.description: The repository's description on GitHub, absent when it has none.

github_id.description: GitHub's id for the repository, empty while it is not yet known.

has_agents_md.description: Whether the repository has an AGENTS.md.

has_claude_md.description: Whether the repository has a CLAUDE.md.

has_readme.description: Whether the repository has a README.

id.description: The repository's id in Triage Factory.

owner.description: The account that owns the repository on GitHub.

profile_text.description: A description of the repository written when it was profiled, absent before then.

profiled_at.description: When the repository was last profiled, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent before then.

repo.description: The repository's name without its owner.

retired_at.description: When the repository was retired because GitHub no longer answers for it, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent on a repository that is not retired.

slug.description: The repository's full name, as owner/name.

base_branch.description: The branch agents base their work on in this repository, or null to clear it so they use the repository's default branch.

body.description: The comment's new text, trimmed of surrounding whitespace, which may not be empty and may not start with a severity badge; the comment keeps the severity it was written with.

dropped.description: How many staged comments were removed because the code they commented on is no longer in the pull request's diff.

head.description: The commit SHA of the pull request's head the review now matches.

moved.description: How many staged comments now sit on a different line or file of the current head.

author.description: The GitHub login of the reviewer.

state.description: The review's state as GitHub spells it, such as APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, DISMISSED, or PENDING.

submitted_at.description: When the review was submitted, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or an empty string for a pending review.

entity_ids.description: The entity ids of the tickets to act on, as the deck lists them: at least one and at most 500, each given once and with no surrounding whitespace.

team_id.description: The id of the caller's team the action is for, whose tracked projects and Jira status rules apply and on which any task is created; when absent it is the team the caller last wrote under, or their one team, and a caller on several teams with neither must give it.

applied.description: How many tickets the action applied to.

failed.description: How many tickets the action did not apply to.

results.description: One result for each submitted entity id, in the order submitted.

assigned.description: The tickets assigned to the caller that have no task, newest first.

available.description: The unassigned tickets in a pickup status that have no task, newest first.

status.description: Whether the lists are filled: ready, or polling, with both lists empty, until Jira's first poll since its configuration last changed has finished.

entity_id.description: The entity id as it was submitted.

errors.description: Why the action did not apply to the ticket, absent when it did.

issue_key.description: The ticket's current Jira key, absent when the entity id names no ticket on the caller's deck.

ok.description: Whether the action applied to the ticket.

bucket.description: Which list the ticket is in: assigned, for a ticket assigned to the caller, or available, for an unassigned ticket in a pickup status.

entity_id.description: The id of the ticket's entity, which the carry-over action routes take.

issue_key.description: The ticket's Jira key, such as PROJ-123.

issue_type.description: The name of the ticket's issue type.

parent_key.description: The Jira key of the ticket's parent issue, absent when it has none.

parent_url.description: The parent issue's page in Jira, absent when the ticket has no parent.

prefilled_action.description: The action the status rules suggest for an assigned ticket from its Jira status: done for a done status, claim for an in-progress one, or queue for a pickup one; absent when no rule matches and on every available ticket.

priority.description: The name of the ticket's priority.

project.description: The key of the ticket's Jira project.

status.description: The name of the ticket's Jira status.

target_user_id.description: The id of the person to hand the task to, which moves the claim another person holds to them; absent, the caller claims the task. It cannot be empty.

team_id.description: The id of the team the caller's own claim puts the task on, one of the task's claim_team_ids; absent when there is only one. It cannot be sent with target_user_id.

version.description: The version the caller's read of the task returned; the claim is refused when the task has changed since. It is required.

dedup_key.description: The value that tells apart tasks of one event type on one entity, such as a label name, which the event must also have; empty for most event types.

entity_id.description: The id of the entity the task is about, which must be active. It is required.

event_type.description: The event type the task is for, which an event recorded on the entity must have. It is required.

team_id.description: The id of the team to create the task for; absent uses the team the caller last wrote to, or their only team.

blueprint_id.description: The id of the blueprint the run carries out, which must belong to the team the task lands on. It is required.

team_id.description: The id of the team the task lands on and the run belongs to, one of the task's claim_team_ids; absent when there is only one.

version.description: The version the caller's read of the task returned; the delegation is refused when the task has changed since. It is required.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation of the run's first step, absent when it could not be read.

status.description: The task's lane after the agent claimed it.

version.description: The task's version after the agent claimed it, which the caller's next write to the task sends.

closed_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits done and dismissed tasks to those closed at or after it.

created_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to tasks created at or after it.

entity_kinds.description: Entity kinds whose tasks to include, such as pr or vulnerable_package; empty includes every kind.

include_snoozed.description: Whether to include tasks still inside their snooze window.

only_unclaimed.description: Whether to include only tasks nobody holds.

sources.description: Sources whose tasks to include, such as github or jira; empty includes every source.

statuses.description: Lanes to include, from queued, in_progress, done, dismissed, and snoozed; empty includes every lane.

team_ids.description: Ids of the teams whose tasks to include; empty includes every team the caller belongs to.

entity_kinds.description: Each entity kind the lane's tasks are about, with how many tasks are about it, counted under every filter in the body except entity_kinds.

event_types.description: Each event type the lane's tasks have, with how many tasks have it, counted under every filter in the body.

ai_summary.description: A summary of the task written when it was scored, absent before then.

autonomy_suitability.description: How suitable the task is for an agent to work without a person, from 0 to 1, or null before the task is scored.

can_write.description: Whether the caller may update, claim, delegate, or requeue the task, present on the task reads and absent from a write's response or when the check fails.

claim_team_ids.description: The ids of the teams the caller's claim or delegation may put the task on, in order, present on the single-task read only and absent when that read fails.

claimed_by_agent_id.description: The id of the agent that holds the task, absent when no agent does.

claimed_by_user_id.description: The id of the person who holds the task, absent when no person does.

close_reason.description: Why the task closed, such as run_completed, user_completed, user_dismissed, or auto_closed_by_event, absent while it is open.

conversation_id.description: The id of the task's current conversation, absent when nobody holds the task or its run has not started.

created_at.description: When the task was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

dedup_key.description: The value that tells apart tasks of one event type on one entity, such as a label name, absent for most event types.

entity_id.description: The id of the entity the task is about: a pull request, an issue, a vulnerable package, or a Slack thread or message.

entity_kind.description: The kind of entity the task is about: pr, issue, vulnerable_package, thread, or message.

event_type.description: The event type that created the task, such as github:pr:review_requested.

memory_attempt.description: The newest attempt to write that memory, absent when none has run.

memory_pending.description: Whether a conversation on the task ended without the memory the next conversation needs, in which case no further conversation on the task starts until that memory exists.

open_subtask_count.description: How many open subtasks the task's Jira issue has, 0 for any other entity.

priority_reasoning.description: The reasoning behind priority_score, absent before the task is scored.

priority_score.description: How urgently the task needs a person's attention, from 0 to 1, or null before the task is scored.

relevance_reason.description: Why the task concerns the person it was routed to, one of review_requested, authored, mentioned, and assigned, absent when none applies.

requested_reviewer.description: On a github:pr:review_requested task, the requested user's login or the requested team's org/slug, absent on every other task.

scoring_status.description: Where the task is in priority scoring: pending, in_progress, or scored.

severity.description: The task's severity, absent when none is recorded.

snooze_until.description: When a snoozed task returns to the queue, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when the task is not snoozed.

source.description: The system the task's entity comes from, such as github or jira.

source_id.description: The entity's key in its source, such as owner/repo#42 for a pull request or PROJ-123 for a Jira issue.

source_url.description: The entity's page in its source.

status.description: The task's lane: queued, in_progress, done, dismissed, or snoozed.

team_id.description: The id of the team that owns the task, absent while no single team owns it.

version.description: The task's version, which a write to the task must send and which each write raises.

vulnerable_package.description: The package and its open Dependabot alerts on a task whose entity_kind is vulnerable_package, absent on every other task.

closed_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits done and dismissed tasks to those closed at or after it.

created_before.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to tasks created at or before it.

created_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to tasks created at or after it.

entity_ids.description: Ids of the entities whose tasks to include, at most 200, each a UUID in lowercase hyphenated form; empty includes every entity.

entity_kinds.description: Entity kinds whose tasks to include, such as pr or vulnerable_package; empty includes every kind.

event_types.description: Event types whose tasks to include, from the catalog GET /api/event-types returns; empty includes every event type.

ids.description: Ids of the tasks to include, at most 200, each a UUID in lowercase hyphenated form; empty includes every task.

include_snoozed.description: Whether to include tasks still inside their snooze window.

only_unclaimed.description: Whether to include only tasks nobody holds.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

search.description: Text the task's title, source id, summary, or event type must contain, matched without regard to case.

sort_dir.description: The direction of sort_key, asc or desc, desc when absent; it is refused without sort_key.

sort_key.description: Orders the result by title, created, event_type, or claimee; absent orders it by the default, open tasks needing attention first and then by priority.

sources.description: Sources whose tasks to include, such as github or jira; empty includes every source.

statuses.description: Lanes to include, from queued, in_progress, done, dismissed, and snoozed; empty includes every lane.

team_ids.description: Ids of the teams whose tasks to include; empty includes every team the caller belongs to.

snooze_until.description: When the task returns to the queue, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in the future, which snoozes an open task nobody holds; null returns a snoozed task to the queue now. It cannot be sent with status.

status.description: The lane to move the task to: done or dismissed, which close it, or in_progress, which needs the caller to hold the task. It cannot be null or sent with snooze_until.

version.description: The version the caller's read of the task returned; the write is refused when the task has changed since. It is required.
The version the caller's read of the task returned; the requeue is refused when the task has changed since. It is required.

id.description: The tool call's id, which the tool message answering it carries as tool_call_id.

input.description: The input the tool is called with.

name.description: The name of the tool called.

next_page_token.description: The token that reads the messages before this page, as page_token, absent when the page reaches the start of the transcript or since_id was given.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache in the category.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache in the category.

category.description: The spend category: manual for runs a person started, autonomous for runs an event handler started, or system_overhead for background jobs.

cost.description: Spend in the category in USD.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens billed in the category.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens billed in the category.

cost.description: Spend on the day in USD.

date.description: The UTC calendar day, as YYYY-MM-DD.

cost.description: Spend on the model on the day in USD.

date.description: The UTC calendar day, as YYYY-MM-DD.

by_day.description: The caller's spend by UTC day.

by_day_model.description: The caller's spend by UTC day and model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_model.description: The caller's spend by model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

total_cost_usd.description: The caller's total spend in the window in USD.

cost.description: Spend on the model in USD.

category.description: The spend category of spend attributed to no team, such as system_overhead.

cost.description: Spend in the category in USD.

by_day.description: The organization's spend by UTC day.

by_day_model.description: The organization's spend by UTC day and model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_model.description: The organization's spend by model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_rule.description: Spend by the event handler that started each run, present only in local mode.

by_user.description: Spend by the person who started each run, across every team.

org_level.description: Spend attributed to no team, by category.

total_cost_usd.description: The organization's total spend in the window in USD, which equals the sum of by_team and org_level.

rule_name.description: The event handler's name, empty when the caller cannot read the handler.

trigger_id.description: The id of the event handler whose runs spent it.

cost.description: Spend attributed to the team in USD.

by_day.description: The team's spend by UTC day.

by_day_model.description: The team's spend by UTC day and model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_model.description: The team's spend by model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_rule.description: The team's spend by the event handler that started each run.

by_user.description: The team's spend by the person who started each run, present only for a team admin, and an empty array when no person has spend in the window.

total_cost_usd.description: The team's total spend in the window in USD.

avatar_url.description: The URL of the person's avatar, absent when they have none.

cost.description: Spend on the person's runs in USD.

user_id.description: The id of the person who started the runs.

alerts.description: The open alerts, highest severity first and then by number.

ecosystem.description: The package's ecosystem, such as npm or pip.

highest_severity.description: The highest severity among the open alerts, one of low, medium, high, and critical, absent when no open alert has one of those.

open_alert_count.description: How many alerts are open on the package.

by.description: The id of the person who requested it.

requested_at.description: When cancellation was requested, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

ids.description: The ids of the rows to request cancellation for, at least one and at most 500.

reason.description: Why the rows are being cancelled, which each row records; it is required and is at most 500 characters once surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

requested.description: How many of the named rows had a cancellation request recorded; a row that has settled or already has a request is not counted.

kinds.description: Every kind of durable work the deployment registers.

cancel.description: Whether cancellation can be requested for the kind's rows.

redrive.description: Whether the kind's parked rows can be redriven.

supersede.description: Whether a parked row of the kind can be superseded by another row.

deferred.description: How many rows are ready but cannot be claimed yet, such as a row whose retry time has not come.

leased.description: How many rows a worker holds.

oldest_deferred_age_seconds.description: The age in seconds, from its first enqueue, of the oldest row counted in deferred, or 0 when there is none.

oldest_ready_age_seconds.description: The age in seconds, from its first enqueue, of the oldest row counted in ready, or 0 when there is none.

parked.description: How many rows are parked, which no worker runs again until an operator redrives or supersedes them.

ready.description: How many of the organization's rows of the kind are ready and can be claimed now.

ids.description: The ids of the parked rows to redrive, at least one and at most 500.

attempt.description: How many attempts have been made on the row since it was enqueued or last redriven.

cancel.description: The cancellation requested for the row, present only when a request is recorded.

created_at.description: When the row was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

done_at.description: When the row was last done, cancelled, or parked, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when none of those has happened since it was enqueued or last redriven.

first_enqueued_at.description: When the row's work was first enqueued, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, which a redrive does not change.

kind.description: The name of the row's kind.

last_error.description: The error the row last recorded, absent when none is recorded.

last_outcome.description: The outcome the row last recorded, such as transient, permanent, budget_exhausted, done, or redriven, absent when none is recorded.

lease.description: The worker's hold on the row, present only while the row is leased.

max_attempts.description: How many attempts the row may have before it is parked.

next_attempt_at.description: The earliest time the row's next attempt may start, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when no retry time is set.

status.description: The row's status: ready, leased, done, parked, or cancelled.

subject.description: What the row is about, in its kind's words, absent when the kind could not describe the row.

superseded_by.description: The id of the row that replaced this one, absent unless the row was superseded.

unique_key.description: The key that keeps a second row for the same work from being enqueued, absent when the row has none.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

status.description: Only rows with this status: ready, leased, done, parked, cancelled, or deferred, which is the ready rows that cannot be claimed yet; absent lists every status.

controls.description: Which operator controls the kind offers.

kind.description: The kind's name, which the kind's routes take in their path.

label.description: The kind's name for a person to read.

epoch.description: The boot count of the process that holds the row, absent when none is recorded.

expires_at.description: When the lease expires unless its holder renews it, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when none is recorded.

generation.description: The lease's generation, a number that rises each time the row is claimed, redriven, or parked.

leased_at.description: When the row was claimed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when none is recorded.

owner.description: The id of the Triage Factory process that holds the row.

oldest_ready_age_seconds.description: How old, in seconds from its first enqueue, the kind's oldest ready row may get before the kind's queue counts as behind.

redriven.description: How many of the named rows returned to ready; a row that was no longer parked is not counted.

detail.description: A longer description, such as the pull request's or issue's title, absent when it is unknown.

fields.description: Further facts about the row by name, such as event_type and entity_id.

label.description: A short name for what the row is about, such as owner/repo#18 for a pull request or PROJ-123 for a Jira issue.

superseded_by.description: The id of the organization's row of the same kind that replaces this one.

superseded.description: 1 when the row was settled as superseded, or 0 when it was no longer parked.

active.description: Whether this is the connection the organization uses in the workspace, which is the one whose events are processed.

app_name.description: The Slack app's bot name, empty when Slack gave none.

bot_user_id.description: The Slack user id of the app's bot.

connection.description: The app's live Socket Mode connection status, absent for an app that receives events over HTTP and before the first connection attempt.

connected_at.description: When the connection last opened, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

consecutive_failures.description: How many connection attempts in a row have failed.

last_error.description: The error of the last failed attempt, absent when there is none.

last_event_at.description: When the connection last received an event, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

sightings.description: Workspaces the app received events from that have no connection in the organization, absent when there are none.

count.description: How many events arrived from the workspace.

last_seen.description: When the last of them arrived, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

state.description: The connection's state: dialing, open, draining, backing_off, or auth_failed.

created_at.description: When the connection was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

enterprise_id.description: The id of the Enterprise Grid organization the workspace belongs to, absent for a standalone workspace.

registered_by_user_id.description: The id of the person who connected the app, absent when that person has since been removed.

source.description: Whose Slack app the connection is through: org for an app the organization created, or deployment for the deployment's own app.

transport.description: How Slack delivers the app's events, socket or events_api, or null on a deployment connection, which uses the transport the deployment configures.

updated_at.description: When the connection was last changed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

session.description: The session cookie a browser sign-in sets. A deployment served over plain HTTP names it sid.

token.description: An API token, sent as Authorization: Bearer tf_….

post.description: Returns one page of the conversations the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and grouped by task id in runs, with each task's newest first. page_size allows up to 500, and total_count counts conversations, not tasks. With include_messages, messages carries the transcript of each task's newest conversation on the page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.
